1284. 1. December. 0. �?0. — Smil von Grotzen bewilligt dem Stifte Hohenfurt in Stadt und District von Gratzen Mauthfreiheit für Wein , Getreide, Fische und andere Dinge.

Legum statuta volunt, ut onтe, quod agatur insolidumper mor tales, testibus idoneis atque fide dignis literarumque apicibus debeat lucidius perelmari. Nos ¡gitur Zmilode Gretzen purchravius in Pode- brad scire volumus universos praesentes literas inspecturos, quod ex dilectione, qua amplectimur fratres religiosos conventus in Alto- vado, porro divinae remunerationis praecipua ratione ipsis in omni bus transducendis suis, quibus ad eorum claustrum potiri videantur, per civitatem nos train Gretzen largam facimus gratiam ex pura volun tate, si ve in vino sive in annona, vel in piscibus aut aliis ductilibus quibuscumque, ut eadem transducant per dictam nostram civitatem Gretzen et citra per »ostros districtus absque teloneo sive muta libere, absque exactione pecuniae aliqualis a nobis. vel a nostris suc- cessivis haeredibus in perpetuum sub tranquillo. Ut autem huic rati- habitioni nullum dubictatis scrupulum valeat suboriri in posterum sive tempore successiva, praesentes ipsis conscribi fecimus in evi- dens testimonium et cautelam sigilli nostri charactere consignatas, testibus subnotatis qui aderant: Ambo nostri patrui videlicet d. entries.english: We, Smilo von Gratzen, Burggraf zu Podebrad, make known that, out of our affection for the religious brothers of the convent at Hohenfurt and for the sake of divine reward, we freely grant them safe passage for all goods transported to their monastery through our town of Gratzen and through our district on this side of it. Whether wine, grain, fish, or any other goods that can be transported, they may carry them freely without toll or customs duty and without any payment to us or our heirs, forever and in peace. We had this charter written and sealed to confirm the grant and prevent any future doubt. Witnesses present: both our uncles, namely Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg and Lord Woko von Witigenow; our kinsman Lord Wocko von Lobenstayn; Lord Albert von Strobnitz; the honorable dean Lord Berthold of Strobnitz; our parish priest Lord Heinrich at Gratzen; our Ritter at Petrinsdorf, Petrus; our steward Paulus; and many others. Done on 1 December 1284. The original charter no longer survives, though it still existed in Millauer’s time, who described its seal as round, hanging, and of white wax, bearing a triangular shield with the familiar rose and the inscription “Seal of Smilo von Gratzen.” Reference: Millauer, p. 88, no. 17.
